subject.title: feat: apply messages.responsePrefix to message tool outbound sends

question: Should `message(action="send")` receive the current agent run's selected provider/model/thinking context for responsePrefix templates, and only for agent-originated visible sends?
rationale: The remaining behavior crosses the reply pipeline, model-selection lifecycle, and message-tool egress contract; source shows no live model selection in the current send path, so automation should not invent that product boundary.

options.title: Support run-context parity
options.body: Thread selected provider/model/thinking context into agent-originated message-tool sends, while keeping out-of-run CLI/generic sends on the current unresolved-template skip behavior.

options.title: Keep static/identity only
options.body: Close the product direction by documenting that message-tool sends can apply only static and identity prefixes because they do not own model selection.

options.title: Move to broader attribution design
options.body: Track model provenance under the broader attribution/fallback work instead of extending responsePrefix on the message-tool path now.

recommendation.title: Support run-context parity
recommendation.body: Thread selected provider/model/thinking context into agent-originated message-tool sends, while keeping out-of-run CLI/generic sends on the current unresolved-template skip behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the shared reply-prefix context and has the strongest history across the reply/outbound boundary where this contract would be decided.
